correctness.rationale: For a complete multipartite graph r≥3 all vertices in different parts are adjacent, those distinct but in the same part have distance 2. Full feedback from a probe in part P yields the robber vertex as a singleton when outside P; if the robber is elsewhere in P, the full set V\P is returned. One cop sweeps P; robber leaving P is immediately located and robber staying in P cannot switch within the same part in one move. Partial feedback: probing all s≤2 vertices of smallest part locates instantly; with s≥3, three probes from distinct parts distinguish each pair of candidate vertices because one probe is adjacent to both and returns the exact candidate. One or two cops below the stated bound always admit distinct candidate vertices x,y from different parts giving identical permissible feedback; after the robber moves N[x]∪N[y]=V resets all contamination, allowing an infinite adversarial response. Correct for all n_i≥1 including complete graphs s=1. Independently checked exact finite-state source and one-round separating probes for small multipartitions; this is corroboration not infinite proof.
residual_risks: Lower bound assumes the precise one-step closed-neighborhood recontamination rules of Jones–Kinnersley; other variants need not share the result. Finite checks through order eight do not prove arbitrarily large parts.

The jump from possibly unbounded min(m,n) for two parts to at most three for three parts is structurally explanatory; winning strategies and matching lower bound, not merely computational samples, give the value.

final_claim: For complete multipartite K_{n1,...,nr} with r≥3 and s=min_i n_i, full-feedback directional localization is 1 and partial-feedback directional localization is min(s,3).
